samples.summary: Partial per-run scores are silently dropped, so the report renders fewer replicates than its own header claims
samples.evidence: Lines 1100-1102 state "a replicate whose score is absent is RECORDED as absent rather than skipped: ... silently dropping one would print a two-replicate range under a three-replicate header". The code immediately does the opposite: `scores[section.key] = perRun.filter(Boolean);` (1108) removes the `null` placeholders, and line 1109 only turns the array into `null` when it is EMPTY. With 2 of 3 `volume-mix-v1` files present, `volumeFigures` receives 2 payloads, `renderVolume` prints `| severity | panel — 2 replicates | ...` and a 2-value range, while the header table at line 677 lists all 3 `--run-id`s as replicates. The range/ratio figures then describe a different K than the document says.

samples.summary: The pooled ratio and CodeRabbit total ignore the `crConsistent` check that the per-severity rows honour
samples.evidence: Per-severity rows guard on consistency: `ratio: crConsistent ? armRatio(...) : notMeasurable("the CodeRabbit arm reads differently across replicates, so it is not one review")` (line 357), and `coderabbit` is given n=0 when inconsistent (356). But the totals do not: `coderabbit_total: figure(replicates[0].coderabbit, 1, "review")` (368) and `pooled_ratio: armRatio(panelTotals, replicates[0].coderabbit)` (369) unconditionally use replicate 0's denominator. So when the arm reads differently across replicates, every severity row correctly says "not measurable" while the bold **total** row still prints a confident ratio built on a denominator the same function just declared unreliable.

samples.summary: Reliability row formatters dereference nested payload fields unguarded — prints `undefined` or throws TypeError on a partially-populated payload
samples.evidence: The comment at 841-844 claims "Every row goes through `renderCell`, so a section whose scorer omitted one figure prints why rather than `undefined`". That only holds when the whole object is absent. `renderValue(rl.recurrence, (rc) => `**${num(rc.in_all.ratio)}** (${rc.in_all.k}/${rc.in_all.n})`)` (847-848) reads `rc.in_all.ratio` with no guard: a `recurrence.overall` that carries `n_classes`/`by_severity` but no `in_all` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`, aborting the whole render (the CLI then exits 1 with no report). Likewise line 845 `(${p.k}/${p.n})` prints the literal string `undefined` when `gate.agreement` exists but lacks `k` — the exact output the test at report.test.mjs:352 believes it has ruled out (it only exercises `gate: {}`, which takes the absent-object path).

samples.summary: `renderCaveats` hard-codes corpus facts (seven items, `pr-524`, "three values") that are not derived from the data being rendered
samples.evidence: Lines 728-731 unconditionally emit "**① One of the seven items is our panel reviewing its own plumbing.** `pr-524` changes ..." and 736-737 emit "every panel column below carries three values rather than one", regardless of `r.corpus_item_ids` or `r.run_ids`. The same file's own header line (664) prints the real item count. Rendered against any other corpus version or a K≠3 run set — which the CLI fully supports via `--corpus-version`/`--run-id` — the report asserts facts about items it did not measure, contradicting its own header table. Same class of hard-coding at line 799 ("contains all three") when `c.bands.length !== 3`.

samples.summary: `worst` is just `bands[0]`; the saturation paragraph quotes one replicate's counts as if they held for all
samples.evidence: `const worst = c.bands[0];` (803) is then used in a sentence introduced by "The ceiling is SATURATED on all ${c.saturated_count} replicates" (805-810), printing `worst.coderabbit_only`, `worst.maybe_links`, `worst.strong_maybe_links` as the queue size. On the fixture the three replicates differ (24/26/25 CodeRabbit-only, 412/420/376 maybe links), so the report attributes replicate 1's numbers to the whole set, and the identifier name asserts a minimum/maximum selection that no code performs.

samples.summary: A reliability payload with no `jaccard` block is rendered as `not-measurable` rather than `not-computed`
samples.evidence: `jaccard: jac && jac.n > 0 ? figure(...) : notMeasurable("no run pair was scorable")`. `jac` is `payload.jaccard?.across_pairs ?? null`, so a payload that simply never emitted the block (an older or truncated scorer output) is reported as structurally impossible to measure — the exact conflation between "nobody measured it" and "it cannot be measured" that AVAILABILITY (lines 108-140) exists to prevent. Contrast the sibling `gate`/`recurrence` fields, which correctly use `notComputed` for an absent block.

samples.summary: `overall` band computes Math.min/Math.max over possibly-empty arrays, yielding Infinity/-Infinity
samples.evidence: `overall: figure({ low: Math.min(...points), high: Math.max(...ceilings) }, points.length, "replicates")`. `points`/`ceilings` are filtered to finite values, and `complementarity.mjs` can legitimately emit `overlap.jaccard === null` (see complementarity.mjs:971, which filters nulls). With every replicate null the cell is `present` with `{low: Infinity, high: -Infinity}` and n=0, rendering as "Across 0 replicates the band is **[n/a, n/a]**" (line 798) — an inverted, meaningless interval presented as a measurement.

samples.summary: Overlap table cells bypass the four-state vocabulary and print a bare `n/a`
samples.evidence: `| ... | ${pct(b.point)} | ${pct(b.ceiling)} | **${band(b.band.value)}** |`. `pct` returns the literal string "n/a" for any non-finite value, and `complementarity.mjs` emits `jaccard: null` when the class total is zero. So a table cell can read "n/a" — neither a measurement nor one of the four availability sentences the module's docblock (lines 41-48) says every cell must be. The `figure()` guard does not catch it because the band value is an object whose fields are unvalidated.

samples.summary: The render path can never exit 0 on today's store: two SECTIONS scorers do not exist, so `missing` is always non-empty
samples.evidence: `process.exitCode = missing.length === 0 ? 0 : 1;` combined with SECTIONS (lines 84-90) containing `cost-latency-v1` (unmerged) and `segmentation-v1` (unbuilt), both of which the loop at 1098-1115 always records as missing. The report is written successfully by `putReport` yet the process exits 1 every time, so any caller that checks the exit status treats the intended, documented output as a failure and cannot distinguish it from a genuinely broken render.

samples.summary: `--json` and `--dry-run` both write to stdout, interleaving JSON and markdown
samples.evidence: Line 1126 `if (args.json) console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));` then line 1137 `process.stdout.write(markdown)` in the dry-run branch. Running `--dry-run --json` emits a JSON document immediately followed by a markdown document on the same stream, so neither can be piped into a parser; the two output modes have no separation (the non-dry-run path is fine because the markdown goes to the store).

samples.summary: `armRatio` only special-cases the literal 0 denominator; a missing/non-numeric CodeRabbit count falls through to division and reports a misleading reason
samples.evidence: `if (codeRabbitCount === 0)` (289) then `spread(vs.map((v) => v / codeRabbitCount))` (294). If `codeRabbitCount` is `undefined`/`null`/NaN (a malformed or renamed volume-mix payload) every ratio is NaN, `spread` filters them all out, `s.n === 0` and the cell says "no panel replicate reported a count for this stratum" (295) — blaming the panel arm for a missing CodeRabbit denominator, which is precisely the mis-attributed absence this module claims to prevent.
